event: Check mcu_intr_handler and the others for counter increments checks.
Checking whether the software trigger drives the count-increment pulse, which decides whether `mcu_intr_handler` exercises item 2.

I submitted the verdict as verified. Four of the five items stand as untested; the "increments by 1 per event" item (`cr_7a8284f75705`) is only partly covered, so I marked it inconclusive.

- **`cr_7a8284f75705`, increments by 1 per event (inconclusive):** `mcu_intr_handler.c` fires one interrupt per software trigger. It compares a firmware count with the sum of the hardware count registers and fails the sim on mismatch. That is a real check of +1 per event, but it is aggregate and goes only through the software trigger path. I read only part of the RTL path from trigger to increment, so I couldn't settle it.
- **`cr_77c7ae0b431e`, rising edge of the hardware event input (verified):** no test drives the hardware event input. The only stimulus is the software trigger register.
- **`cr_81ffd1fa635f`, 1-cycle pulse (verified):** no test checks the pulse width.
- **`cr_84e8df210e83` and `cr_8a0bed11bd11`, saturation (verified):** no test drives a counter to `0xffffffff`. The RTL does implement the saturation.

I found no other test that reads or checks these counters. The coverage file and `libs/mci/mci.c` only list the registers.
